meta.subject: Physics
meta.lessonTitle: What Is Pressure? Measuring the Invisible Push

quiz.prompt: A book and a pencil are pressed onto your palm with the same force. Why does the pencil tip hurt more?
choices: The pencil is heavier than the book
The same force acts on a much smaller area, so the pressure is greater
The pencil pushes with a bigger force
The book spreads the force over a smaller area
quiz.rationale: P = F/A. With F the same, a smaller contact area gives a larger pressure. The masses and forces were deliberately kept equal.
quiz.placement: Formal definition P = F/A, after the book vs pencil demonstration

quiz.prompt: A shoe sole covers 150 cm². What is this area in square metres?
quiz.rationale: 1 m² = 10 000 cm², so 150 ÷ 10 000 = 0.015 m². This conversion is the error the lesson plan flags as most common.
quiz.placement: Part B: shoe-pressure investigation (cm² to m² conversion)

quiz.prompt: A maize bag on a pallet pushes 225 N onto each leg. Each leg touches the floor over 0.0025 m², so the pressure is 90 000 ____. Which unit completes the answer?
quiz.rationale: Pressure = force ÷ area, so its unit is N/m², called the pascal (Pa). Newton is force, kg is mass, m² is area.
quiz.placement: Problem 1: maize bag on a pallet (Eldoret warehouse)

quiz.prompt: A rungu tip (2 cm²) and a crutch base (50 cm²) each press down with 150 N. Which statement is correct?
choices: They exert the same pressure because the force is the same
The crutch exerts higher pressure because it is larger
The rungu exerts higher pressure because its area is smaller
Neither exerts pressure because they are not moving
quiz.rationale: Rungu: 150 ÷ 0.0002 = 750 000 Pa. Crutch: 150 ÷ 0.005 = 30 000 Pa. Same force, smaller area, much higher pressure. So the crutch is safer on a soft floor.

quiz.prompt: In which directions does atmospheric pressure push on the jerrycan?
choices: Inward on every surface: top, bottom and all sides
quiz.rationale: Atmospheric pressure acts on every exposed surface, from all directions. The lesson plan flags students who draw arrows only on top as holding a key misconception.
